sources.entry: Jelu - Read and to-read list book tracker. (Source Code) MIT Java/Docker

summary.one_liner: Jelu is a self-hosted personal book tracker (a "personal Goodreads") for logging books you have read, are reading, or want to read.
summary.what_it_does: Jelu tracks read, currently-reading, finished, dropped, and to-read books, with history viewable by year and month. Books can be tagged, and tags can be used to build custom shelves and tag pages. It imports Goodreads CSV exports or ISBN lists and exports data to CSV, and it can search online by title, author, or ISBN to add books automatically. The README also describes author pages with Wikipedia details, review writing and sharing, embeddable tracking snippets, reading stats, multi-user support (LDAP, proxy auth), and an API. Data is kept in a single-file SQLite database.
use_cases: track books I have read and want to read
replace Goodreads with a self-hosted alternative
script or integrate reading data through an API
share book reviews with other users on my instance
how_to_run: Download the Jelu jar from the releases section into a dedicated folder
Optionally create application.yml next to the jar to change settings such as the database path
Open the web UI at localhost:11111
Docker: use the image wabayang/jelu with a compose file mapping /config, /database, /files/images, /files/imports and port 11111
notable: Single-file SQLite database that can be saved anywhere
Optional WAL journal mode for concurrent use on local disks
Automatic metadata search via calibre's fetch-ebook-metadata
Multi-user support with LDAP or proxy authentication
caveats: Automatic online metadata search depends on the external calibre fetch-ebook-metadata tool when run as a Java jar
WAL journal mode should not be used on network shares such as NFS or SMB
Backups must include all jelu.db* files when WAL mode is on, or Jelu must be stopped first
